content.title: About
content.content: The Fried Seafood Sandwich is a crispy roll or bun filled with battered and fried shrimp, calamari, fish, and sometimes scallops, complemented by fresh vegetables and a tangy tartar or mayo sauce. It combines a crunchy exterior with tender, flavorful seafood.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in coastal U.S. towns in the 1970s as a street‑food staple.
A beer‑based batter is often used to give the coating extra lightness and aroma.
In Japan the sandwich is known as "エビフライサンド" (Ebi Fry Sand).
It is traditionally served with a lemon wedge to highlight the seafood freshness.
Some restaurants add a seaweed mix for an extra oceanic flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp and fish provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: Fatty fish in the sandwich supplies omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

items.title: Rich in minerals and vitamins
items.content: Seafood delivers zinc, selenium, vitamin B12, and vitamin D, important for immunity and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with a light batter and healthy oil, the sandwich can be less fatty than typical meat options.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Taurine and other amino acids in seafood help accelerate metabolic processes.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, shellfish, or fish.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared batters and sauces often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Risk of over‑eating
items.content: Fried foods can be calorie‑dense; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species may contain mercury; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, cut in half. It pairs well with fresh lettuce, pickles, or a drizzle of chili sauce. For a lighter version, use a whole‑grain bun and bake the seafood instead of frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best enjoyed immediately. If needed, wrap tightly in foil and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Fried seafood can be stored separately in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheated in the oven to retain crispness.
